Backends: how a prompt becomes a response

Source: R/backends.R
backends.Rd

A backend is a function function(prompt, model, row) that sends prompt to model and returns the raw text response (a length-one character vector). row is the corresponding row of the design and can be ignored. A backend may instead return a list with elements text and meta; meta (a named list, e.g. token counts or the model snapshot id reported by the API) is stored with the run. Any client library can be wrapped this way; three backends are provided.

Usage

backend_mock(
  truth,
  levels = NULL,
  thresholds = NULL,
  sd_prompt = 0.2,
  sd_model = 0.2,
  sd_rep = 0.3,
  p_fail = 0,
  template = "The result is: %s.",
  seed = NULL
)

backend_ellmer(chats)

backend_openai_compatible(
  base_url = "https://api.openai.com/v1",
  api_key = Sys.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"),
  temperature = 0,
  system = NULL,
  max_tokens = NULL,
  timeout = 120,
  ...
)

Arguments

truth

A named vector giving the latent true value of every item_id (numeric). For ordinal mocks this is the latent position; the label is obtained by cutting at thresholds.

levels

Optional ordered labels. If given, the mock returns a label; otherwise it returns a number.

thresholds

Cut points on the latent scale (length length(levels) - 1).

sd_prompt, sd_model, sd_rep

Standard deviations of the prompt effect, the model effect and the replicate noise on the latent scale. Prompt and model effects are drawn once per prompt id / model id and kept fixed.

p_fail

Probability that the mock returns an unparseable response, to exercise failure handling.

template

A sprintf-style sentence with one %s for the value.

seed

Seed for the mock's private random number stream.

chats

For backend_ellmer(): an ellmer Chat object, or a named list of Chat objects keyed by model id.

base_url, api_key, temperature, system, max_tokens, timeout, ...

For backend_openai_compatible(): server URL (without the trailing /chat/completions), API key (may be empty for local servers), sampling temperature, optional system message, token limit, request timeout in seconds, and further fields merged into the JSON body. temperature = NULL omits the temperature field. A non-empty, non-NA row$system overrides system and precedes the user message. The reply's id, model (as model_snapshot), usage, system_fingerprint (including null) and optional provider are recorded in meta. A reasoning text in message.reasoning (as some OpenRouter endpoints return it) is recorded as reasoning when it is a non-empty string; otherwise the key is absent. reasoning_details is not stored. finish_reason and native_finish_reason of the first choice are recorded under these names when they are non-empty strings, so that a reply cut at the token limit can be told apart from an unreadable one. Requested routing is recorded as provider_order, quantizations and allow_fallbacks. Requested seed, temperature and reasoning_effort, when present, are retained as metadata for comparison with the study plan, and the request timeout as timeout_s. Only message.content is parsed; credentials and headers are not stored.

Value

A backend function.

Details

  • backend_mock() simulates an LLM for examples, tests and teaching. The default simulation draws a latent score from the item's truth plus prompt, model and replicate noise and writes a short sentence that contains the resulting label or number, so that the whole chain from prompt to parser can be exercised offline.

  • backend_ellmer() wraps one or several ellmer chat objects (one per model id). Each call uses a fresh clone, so no conversation history leaks between calls.

  • backend_openai_compatible() talks to any server that implements the OpenAI chat-completions API: OpenAI itself, Ollama (base_url = "http://localhost:11434/v1"), vLLM, LM Studio, Azure-style proxies.

Examples

truth <- c(v1 = 1.2, v2 = -0.4)
bk <- backend_mock(truth, levels = c("Benign", "VUS", "Pathogenic"),
                   thresholds = c(-0.5, 0.5), seed = 1)
bk("Classify v1", "model-a", list(item_id = "v1", prompt_id = "P1", model_id = "model-a"))
#> $text
#> [1] "The result is: VUS."
#> 
#> $meta
#> $meta$mock
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $meta$latent
#> [1] 0.3877586
#> 
#>
